newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian fund investors shedding equity aversion.
newsitem.headline: Indian fund investors shedding equity aversion.

text.p: Overcautious mutual fund investors who had parked all their investments in debt last year when the equities market crashed are slowly shifting some of their portfolio into equities, fund managers said on Wednesday.

"The extreme caution which people displayed earlier this year by not allocating any funds to equity at all -- that's gradually changing," Ajai Kaul, country manager of Alliance Capital Asset Management Company told Reuters.

"But investors are not rushing from debt to equity," he added. "Every investor has a comfort level. It's just that the excess of funds put into debt earlier this year when equities were faring badly are beginning to flow back."
Alliance Capital is the Indian subsidiary of Alliance Capital Management LP of the U.S.
Officials at Birla Capital Asset Mangement Company, another private mutual fund, said it was too early to talk about a shift in favour of equities.
When its fund Birla Income Plus invested one percent of its funds in equity earlier this year, many of its investors were unhappy and the fund decided to revert to 100 percent debt.
An official of Kothari Mutual Fund, the Indian affiliate of U.S. fund Pioneer Inc, said investors appeared to be slightly more optimistic on equities, as compared to the early part of the year.
"But it has not translated into more investment in equities. It may happen after a time lag," he said.
Kothari Pioneer is the Indian affiliate of Pioneer Group Inc of the U.S.
A host of mutual funds dedicated to investment in fixed income instruments came up early this year, taking advantage of investors' disenchantment with falling stock markets.
The 30-share benchmark index of the Bombay Stock Exchange fell to a three-year low of 2,713.12 points in December 1996.
Stock markets have been rising in recent months, powered by large inflows from foreign institutional investors.
The 30-share Bombay Stock Market index was at 4,511.64 points on Wednesday afternoon.
